findings.F1: Sense 1 grammar pattern 'verb + to-infinitive' is wrong; must takes a bare infinitive.
findings.F2: Obligation example 'You must hand in your homework by Friday.' sits under the 'almost certainly true' sense.
findings.F4: The no-past/had to fact and the must not vs don't have to contrast are repeated across explanation, usage note, learner errors and grammar adaptation.
findings.F5: The cannot/can't-as-opposite fact for sense 2 is stated in the explanation, the compare note and the semantic adaptation.
findings.F6: The have to compare note restates the sense 1 explanation.
findings.F7: shall-modal listed as a synonym of must though it means obligation only in legal or formal writing.
findings.F8: Must not and do not have to are called 'opposite'; they are different in meaning, not opposites.
findings.F9: see_also duplicates the sense 1 compare items (have-v, should-modal).
findings.F10: The frequent emphatic use 'I must say / I must admit' is not covered.
findings.F11: The 'if you must' phrase explanation only restates its definition.
findings.F12: The grammar adaptation says must has no past form without limiting this to obligation, though must have done expresses past deduction.
